title: ACRS on AppWorld: development split, first full run
source: Kaggle notebook acrs-paim-dev-pilot, Version 2 (seven configurations, 10 h 32 min) and Version 3 (without O3, 131 min), 2 x T4; harness github.com/joyjeni/acrs-appworld, branch o4-provenance
privacy: Aggregates only. AppWorld task text and API outputs are not published.

models.serving: vLLM on two free T4 GPUs, thinking mode off

objectives.name: Session-Adaptive Tool Scoring
objectives.appworld: BM25 over the instruction and the last two code blocks, boosted by a decaying memory of the apps the episode used; committed APIs stay visible; login docs only for apps not yet logged in.

objectives.name: PID-Controlled Provenance Pruning
objectives.appworld: Task and last three steps kept verbatim; older steps become one outline line each: errors kept, short outputs kept, outputs still held by a live variable become a pointer, the rest cut to a length a PID controller sets.

objectives.name: Risk-Weighted Policy Routing
objectives.appworld: Two-arm contextual Thompson sampler picks Qwen3-4B or Qwen3-8B per step; on a risky context the small model must beat the large one by a margin of 0.35; the large model carries a cost penalty of 0.15.

objectives.name: Byzantine-Tolerant Coordination for Certified Execution
objectives.appworld: On a state-changing step, three candidate programs run from a saved world state; the outcome is executed for real only if at least two agree (share 0.5 or more); otherwise ACRS abstains.

objectives.name: Policy as code (approve before execute)
objectives.appworld: Denies deletions the instruction does not ask for, writes to apps outside the task's scope, and ids or e-mail addresses the agent never observed.

code_names.note: The released harness uses the earlier objective numbering.

configs.label: Reference agent
configs.description: ReAct-style agent on the same models: 8B model on every step, recent-history window, no ACRS component

configs.label: Full without O1
configs.description: Retrieval once from the instruction, never updated

configs.label: Full without O2
configs.description: Recent-history window instead of provenance pruning

configs.label: Full without O4
configs.description: Single greedy proposal executed, no vote

findings.evidence: 17.5 % against 10.5 % task success without O1 (7 tasks against 3, McNemar p = 0.344); wrong-API errors not lower.
findings.next: Offline recall test: does the shown documentation contain the API the reference solution calls next?

findings.evidence: Median prompt tokens per task down 23 % (17,263 against 22,413, Wilcoxon p = 0.0013); repeated API calls 1,465 to 302; recoverability 0.80 to 0.97; success unchanged (p = 0.625).
findings.next: Confirm on the test splits with three seeds.

findings.status: Cost claim supported; risk check pending
findings.evidence: 21.8 % of steps on the 4B model; 448 calls to the 8B model against 570 for the same system without O3 (21 % fewer) and 873 for the reference agent; success 17.5 % against 14.0 % without O3 (2 tasks against 0, McNemar p = 0.5).
findings.next: Per-step check, from the saved logs, that risky steps went to the 8B model.

findings.evidence: No collateral damage with O4 against 1 of 57 tasks without it; 2.4 times the tokens and 2.6 times the wall time; G1 never fired. With three candidates per vote the quorum bound tolerates no faulty candidate, so this vote is an agreement check, not a Byzantine guarantee.
findings.next: Tasks with planted faults and unsafe instructions, votes with at least four candidates, and a cheaper vote.

findings.evidence: No configuration significantly better on success; full ACRS completes 3 of 19 scenarios against 1 for the reference agent.
findings.next: Reference agent and full ACRS on test_normal and test_challenge, three seeds (about 155 paired tasks detect a 10-point difference).

caveats: Single seed: full ACRS and full ACRS without G1 behave identically (G1 never fired) yet differ by 5.2 points, which is run-to-run noise.
57 tasks detect only large effects; about 155 paired tasks are needed to detect a 10-point difference in task success.
Development split with 4-bit 4B/8B models and three worked examples: not comparable with leaderboard entries on test_normal.
context: Strongest AppWorld entries (November 2026) complete 91 to 94 % of test_normal tasks with frontier models; the best entry with a model of at most 14B parameters reaches 86.9 %. ACRS is compared first with the reference agent on the same models.
next_runs: Per-step analysis of the router's choices on risky steps (from the saved logs, no GPU)
Reference agent and full ACRS on test_normal and test_challenge with three seeds

security_controls.rule: A delete-type call runs only if the task asks to delete or remove.
Writes only to apps the task allows.
An id, e-mail address or phone number written by a state-changing call must have been observed in the task or an earlier result.
Commit an answer only when it is certified, the quorum holds, no quarantined evidence is used and no stage failed (fail closed).
A peer may call only a read-only tool that O1 committed for the sub-goal (least privilege).
A state-changing tool runs only after a named person approved that exact call.
Only successful, non-quarantined observations enter the next turn's context and O1's session prior (blocks injected text from persisting).
A release is promoted by a named approver after the evaluation gate passed on a pinned manifest.
